dedupe_keys.name: critical mineral mines tied to violent incidents and protests 2021 2023 global witness 2024

description: This investigation by Global Witness links mining of four energy transition minerals, copper, cobalt, lithium and nickel, to incidents of violence and protest in the ten countries that produce most of each mineral. It combines S&P Global data on mine locations, production and the nationality of mining companies with conflict and protest events from ACLED, and classifies countries with the International Monetary Fund's economic groups. It was published by Global Witness on 7 November 2024, with the partners AFREWATCH and JATAM, who helped build an interactive tool showing production growth, company nationalities, active mines and ACLED events. Coverage is the top ten producing countries for each mineral over 2021 to 2023. The report is available online free as a 4.4 MB PDF in English and a Chinese version; the page states no licence. Findings: 334 incidents, about 111 a year, with nearly 90% in emerging and developing economies, while companies from advanced and major consumer economies control 71% to 81% of production. Caveats: it is advocacy research, the underlying S&P data are commercial, and event counts depend on ACLED's coverage and on how events are matched to mines. For simulation it shows where social unrest could interrupt mineral supply for batteries, grids and renewables, supporting resilience and supply risk scenarios such as price spikes after riots. It is related to the WRI global mining in socially vulnerable areas record in this catalogue.
